terms.title: Quantum Relativity (QR)
terms.status: D; H for the proposed physical theory
terms.section: I. Identity, scope, and native objects
terms.body:
Quantum Relativity is a theory of relational complexity governed by conservation of information. It studies registered relational organizations and the admissible transductions through which their distinctions propagate, remain retained, become comparable, and acquire history. "Quantum Relativity is transducer theory" remains the compact operational description, not a competing definition.

The subject is relational complexity; the constraint is complete information accounting; the mechanism is admissible transduction. The quantum and geometric readings are proposed reductions of this architecture, not two already-proved physical theories joined merely by terminology. QR does not require a wavefunction or spacetime manifold as its starting ontology, but can use either in a declared mathematical representation.

This definition names a research program. It does not make every proposed complexity functional, source law, instrument, or physical correspondence an established consequence of the Thalion. See [[relational-complexity]], [[information-conservation]], and [[unification]].

terms.title: Thalean
terms.status: D; historical naming rationale
terms.section: I. Identity, scope, and native objects
terms.body:
"Thalean" names the program's commitment to explanation through natural principle rather than caprice, with Thales of Miletus and "everything is water" retained as the author's historical naming background. Water is not thereby asserted to be the literal substrate of QR, and the name is not an argument for the equations.

The secondary Tolkien resonance associated with "Thalion" is an authorial mnemonic for steadfastness or informational fidelity. It is neither the mathematical derivation of the object nor evidence for a physical correspondence. These naming notes belong to the program's introduction; they do not add operators, degrees of freedom, or empirical laws.

The operative use of the adjective is domain-specific: a Thalean statement concerns a declared object, action, construction, or hypothesis in this program. "Thalean" is not itself a proof-status label.

terms.title: Thalean graph
terms.status: D; inherited carrier identification
terms.section: I. Identity, scope, and native objects
terms.body:
The Thalean graph is the full graph-level organism or object-class under discussion, centrally represented in this program by AT4val[60,6]. The name must not drift to a quotient, matrix, or visual rendering simply because that shadow is easier to display.

A graph designation, a concrete structured instance, and a functional description have different roles. AT4val[60,6] is the graph designation; Thalion is the object name; Thalean Transducer is the proposed functional name. These names can refer to the same native object while emphasizing different aspects of it.

The G15 sector system, M_sec, Q_sec, and its cubic overlap law are downstream legibility layers. They do not replace the full G60 object or automatically retain its signed-lift, transport, closure, and registration information. See [[thalion]] and [[quotient-shadow]].

terms.title: Thalion / one thalion / Thalean Transducer
terms.status: D; native properties retain their individual source statuses
terms.section: I. Identity, scope, and native objects
terms.body:
A thalion is one concrete functional cluster-instance of the G60 form AT4val[60,6], including its full relevant relationships and properties. Thalean Transducer is the functional name for that object considered through what its admitted operations distinguish, propagate, retain, compare, close, and register.

The statement that "G60 is the carrier" is a way to separate bare graph data from the additional structures being used in an argument. It is not a redefinition of a thalion as G15, a selected eigenspace, one vertex, or a freely decorated unrelated graph. Only explicitly supplied or derived structures belong to the admitted construction; proposed apparatus choices and physical readings remain separately marked.

"One thalion" is an instance-level unit, not a universal scalar of complexity, action, time, or information. Its finite state set does not imply that every possible ordered history of repeated use is finite in length. See [[extensible-history]].

terms.title: QR transducer
terms.status: D
terms.section: I. Identity, scope, and native objects
terms.body:
A QR transducer is a local relational system with a declared input domain, admission constraints, input-output operation, retained register, and any handoff interface required by its task. It identifies which continuations are admissible and realizes an admitted transformation; this does not mean that bare geometry already determines a unique next outcome.

The complete-input notation is:

```text
T_e : (x,m) -> (p,m')
```

Here x is incoming payload, m is prior local memory, p is propagated or onward-eligible output, and m' is the complete retained output. The abbreviation x -> (p,r) is safe only when x already includes the complete input and r includes all retained output needed for recovery.

A generic QR transducer need not be identified with the particular G60 Thalion. A native Thalean realization must provide the relevant carrier, admission rule, recovery map, and interface rather than merely adopt this input-output shape.

terms.title: History-bearing transducer
terms.status: D; mechanism-specific C/H
terms.section: I. Identity, scope, and native objects
terms.body:
A history-bearing transducer is one whose future admitted response depends on retained distinctions produced by earlier events. It is more than a finite machine accompanied by a passive external log: some retained distinction must actually enter the future admission or response law.

The local carrier can remain finite while an extensible register stores a growing history. But when that register affects the controller, it is part of the complete dynamical state; the total effective state is then not confined to the fixed finite carrier alone. This clarifies the baseline's finite-carrier/extensible-history language without claiming unbounded memory is contained inside finitely many vertices.

The operational test is [[informative-coupling]] or [[predictive-history]]: hold the other relevant context fixed and show a difference in available future tests or registered responses. A stored distinction that never participates in such a test is archival evidence, not established dynamical feedback.

terms.title: Native, admitted, and supplied structure
terms.status: D; provenance discipline
terms.section: I. Identity, scope, and native objects
terms.body:
"Native" means construction-derived from the declared source object and permitted operations, with the dependencies needed to reconstruct that derivation. "Admitted" means included in a specified grammar or contract. "Supplied" means taken as input. These roles can overlap, but they are not synonyms.

An algebraically definable operator is not automatically an admitted event. An admitted apparatus hypothesis is not automatically selected uniquely by the graph. A supplied representation can support an exact conditional theorem while leaving its native origin open. Each entry must identify which level is being used.

The independence requirement is crucial: a source, weight, or selection law cannot be called derived merely because it was chosen to reproduce the target Born table or another desired answer. Provenance records what constructs the object before the target comparison, as well as what was tested afterward.

terms.title: Carrier and representation
terms.status: D
terms.section: I. Identity, scope, and native objects
terms.body:
A carrier is the specified domain on which an action, state, relation, or readout is defined. It may be a finite set, graph, quotient, groupoid, history language, vector space, or operator module. A statement is incomplete when it names an operator but leaves its carrier unspecified.

For a finite set X, the linearized carrier R^X has a basis indexed by X. Its dimension equals |X|, but arbitrary subspaces of R^X are not automatically subsets of X. In particular a 7,200-dimensional harmonic subspace is not a demonstrated 7,200-element receipt set.

A representation encodes an admitted structure on another carrier. Faithfulness, preservation of products, preservation of inner products, and compatibility with readout are distinct properties. An isomorphism of abstract groups does not identify their concrete state actions. See [[intertwiner]] and the symbol register.

terms.title: Quotient-visible shadow and compressed legibility
terms.status: D
terms.section: I. Identity, scope, and native objects
terms.body:
A quotient-visible shadow is information retained by a specified projection or compression of a richer relational object. It is useful precisely because it forgets distinctions that the intended readout does not need. It should not be treated as a complete reconstruction unless sufficiency has been proved.

Examples include G60 -> G30 -> G15, the sector incidence M_sec, and Q_sec = M_sec M_sec^T. A scalar, Gram matrix, or projective axis can preserve an invariant while erasing lift orientation, phase, incidence, or order of execution.

Apparent loss under projection is compatible with information conservation of the complete event. The missing distinction must remain in another output or retained register if recovery requires it. Equal quotient values therefore do not imply equal complete states, equal histories, or equal future responses.

terms.title: Complete comparison context
terms.status: D
terms.section: I. Identity, scope, and native objects
terms.body:
A comparison context is the collection of conditions held fixed when admissibility, response, freedom, or informativeness is evaluated. It includes the relevant current state, retained variables, preparation, apparatus setting, reference presentation, and allowed test family. "Complete" is relative to that declared test, not a claim to know the whole universe.

Changing a passive reference can change coordinates without changing the underlying admitted relation. Changing an apparatus constraint can change the relation itself. Those two operations must not be hidden under the same word "context."

Expressions such as Adm(z), P(x | Ctx,Ref), and O_(z,r)(w) should therefore name what is fixed and what is varied. This is especially important for the retained-history actuator, freedom carry-forward, and contextual EPR readouts.

terms.title: Relation
terms.status: D
terms.section: II. Possibility, action, events, and historical registration
terms.body:
A relation is a locally available connection between distinguishable states, interfaces, or transducers through which an admissible event could occur. Adjacency is one concrete representation; a typed interaction interface is another. The compact reading is "relation = available possibility."

Availability is not transmission. A carrier edge can show that an interaction is possible in principle while a context-dependent admission domain determines whether the present input can use it. Relation therefore precedes realized action without being an unrestricted promise that every imaginable transformation is allowed.

The definition is used operationally: identify the endpoints, the interface or incidence, and the relevant admission conditions. The richer philosophical claim that objects are persistent relational organizations belongs to the QR interpretation, not a substitute for supplying those data in a finite construction.

terms.title: Possibility, actuality, and impossibility
terms.status: D
terms.section: II. Possibility, action, events, and historical registration
terms.body:
A possibility is a continuation compatible with the current declared constraints. An actuality is a realized event. An impossible continuation is excluded by those constraints. "Did not occur" is not equivalent to "was impossible before the event."

The double-slit discussion fixes the realized occurrence as singular while retaining a plural family of admissible alternatives before registration. This is the adopted QR reading of actuality; it does not by itself derive an interference experiment or a unique outcome-selection mechanism.

A counterfactual must retain its time and context. An alternative that was permitted at one prefix can cease to be a possible extension of the realized history afterward. That does not retroactively make its earlier permission false. See [[foreclosure]] and [[continuation-family]].

terms.title: Admissibility and permissible action
terms.status: D
terms.section: II. Possibility, action, events, and historical registration
terms.body:
Admissibility is satisfaction of the declared native relational constraints for a continuation or transduction. Permissible action denotes the allowed action family, including the structure that distinguishes and relates its alternatives. It need not be a scalar probability distribution.

For a specified context z, write Adm(z) for the family of admitted elementary continuations. Additional registration or retained history can refine this family, but a passive renaming of a reference must not manufacture permission. Recoverability and handoff conditions remain separate explicit requirements where they are part of the event contract.

Admissibility is not designation or realization. The finite routing example gives one forbidden and two lawful continuations at each relevant directed quotient edge. The graph's permission law alone does not choose between the lawful pair. See [[designation]] and [[routing-permission]].

terms.title: Continuation
terms.status: D
terms.section: II. Possibility, action, events, and historical registration
terms.body:
A continuation is a lawful possible next relation or admitted elementary operation available from the present relational and registration context. It remains a possibility until it is realized.

The term also extends to an admitted word of future operations, provided the length and composition grammar are stated. An immediate successor, a whole future path, and a completed history are different objects. A count of successors is not automatically a count of independent degrees of freedom, and a count of paths is not automatically a probability measure.

A continuation must be compared on a common domain. If two histories permit different future languages, that difference already matters to predictive state even before any common test produces different outputs. See [[predictive-history]], [[continuation-multiplicity]], and [[freedom]].

terms.title: Designation and selection
terms.status: D; native selector remains mechanism-specific
terms.section: II. Possibility, action, events, and historical registration
terms.body:
Designation specifies which member of an admissible family is selected, named, or assigned for an execution. When designation means a dynamical choice rather than a label convention, the actual selecting mechanism must be supplied. Naming a branch b rather than ab is not the same as causing it to occur.

The canonical separation is:

```text
permission != designation != realization != registration
```

Geometry can determine a lawful pair without choosing a member. A retained variable can influence the choice without proving a complete autonomous source law. A receipt can identify the member that occurred without having selected it upstream.

This distinction prevents a fitted scheduler, a chosen orientation section, or a post hoc history classification from being silently promoted into the law of becoming. The glossary records the source-law frontier rather than filling it by definition.

terms.title: Informative action and realized action
terms.status: D
terms.section: II. Possibility, action, events, and historical registration
terms.body:
Informative action is an admissible realized continuation that creates or changes a registered relational distinction. Informativeness is relative to a specified registration or future-response family: the action must have a distinguishable consequence in that family, not merely be assigned a new name.

The phrase "action is always real" concerns realized action. An admissible action type or member of Adm(z) can be discussed before it is realized; that use names a possible operation. Keeping the type/occurrence distinction resolves the otherwise circular phrase "set of realized actions available before realization."

A return with unchanged projected endpoint can still be informative through its retained residue. Conversely preservation of a scalar invariant alone does not establish an informative effect. This primitive use of action is distinct from a dimensionful mechanical action functional S_mech[gamma] and from a proposed hbar calibration.

terms.title: Admissible transduction
terms.status: D; P for injectivity/recovery equivalence on a declared finite domain
terms.section: II. Possibility, action, events, and historical registration
terms.body:
An admissible transduction is a local transformation of a complete incoming relational state that satisfies the declared constraints and preserves the information needed for reconstruction from its complete output. It reorganizes information between onward output and retained output rather than authorizing unaccounted erasure.

```text
T_e : D_e -> P_e x R_e
Rec_e o T_e = id_(D_e)
```

The recovery identity is required on the admitted image. Surjectivity onto every abstract pair in P_e x R_e is unnecessary. If prior memory participates in the operation, recovery must reconstruct that memory as well as the new payload.

In a coherent representation, an analogous complete-output condition is an isometry V_e with V_e^dagger V_e = I. Using this representation does not independently derive a quantum instrument or its physical interpretation. See [[recoverability]] and [[complete-input]].

terms.title: QR event
terms.status: D; propagation-sector qualification made explicit
terms.section: II. Possibility, action, events, and historical registration
terms.body:
In the propagation sector, a QR event is one completed, receipted, admissible relational handoff. It comprises an admitted local transduction, the corresponding adjacent address acquisition, and the complementary retained accounting required for that completed occurrence. "Event = informative action + historical registration" describes its occurrence/record aspect rather than a separate competing definition.

The baseline repeatedly defined every event as an adjacent handoff. The later manuscript explicitly distinguishes internal registration actions from field displacements. This edition keeps the original strict meaning as the propagation-event definition and uses "internal registered action" for completed local occurrences that have no established address increment. It does not count every internal algebraic update as transmission.

The realized occurrence is singular in the adopted double-slit framing. Its event type can remain invariant across several presentations without making those presentations separate occurrences or identifying distinct occurrences with one another.

terms.title: Adjacent handoff
terms.status: D
terms.section: II. Possibility, action, events, and historical registration
terms.body:
An adjacent handoff is the completed transfer of the propagated component across exactly one admitted neighboring field relationship. It is the primitive local unit of propagation used in the current c_Th normalization.

The adjacency must belong to the declared transducer field, and the present payload must satisfy its handoff domain. A graph path drawn between labels is not enough. The complete output must also retain whatever complementary distinctions make the handoff recoverable and accountable.

Handoff is narrower than arbitrary state change. Internal phase updates, reference changes, or receipt writes can be real operations without having moved a payload to a new field address. A multi-edge process must not be reclassified as one primitive handoff solely to change its apparent causal slope. See [[event-depth]] and [[thalean-c]].

terms.title: Propagated component
terms.status: D
terms.section: II. Possibility, action, events, and historical registration
terms.body:
The propagated component is the output eligible to acquire an adjacent field address under the admitted handoff rule. It is what continues across that interface, not necessarily everything that was present in the incoming state.

Recovery belongs to the complete propagated-plus-retained output. The propagated component may therefore be insufficient by itself: two distinct inputs can have the same onward component while their receipts distinguish them. If the onward component already identifies the complete input, the recovery receipt may be trivial.

The phrase "the propagated component moves" describes this interface role. It does not establish that a scalar complexity value, electric charge, energy, or a physical particle has moved unless the relevant encoding, transport, and decoding are separately supplied.

terms.title: Trace
terms.status: D
terms.section: II. Possibility, action, events, and historical registration
terms.body:
A trace is a retained relational consequence of informative action. It is the broad term for what the occurrence leaves available to later recording or comparison.

A trace becomes a receipt in the stronger accounting sense only when its specified content, together with the other complete outputs, is sufficient for the required distinction or reconstruction. A trace can be partial, coarse, or visible only through a later readout. Its existence alone does not establish a future feedback mechanism.

This term is distinct from the matrix trace Tr(A), which sums diagonal entries and is used in spectral normalization. The shared English word does not identify a physical historical record with a linear-algebra scalar. Write "event trace" or "matrix trace" when both occur nearby.

terms.title: Retained receipt
terms.status: D
terms.section: II. Possibility, action, events, and historical registration
terms.body:
A retained receipt is a complementary distinction required, together with the propagated component and relevant retained memory, to account for a completed admissible transduction or handoff. It is part of the complete output, not waste and not a license to discard the input distinction.

"Retained" identifies its accounting role. Depending on the construction, the receipt can remain local, be encoded in a carrier, or later be transported. The baseline's shorthand "the receipt stays" should not be read as a universal permanent immobility theorem. A receipt can also be trivial when the onward output is already sufficient.

A generic receipt is not automatically a spin residue, a scalar duration, a probability, or an externally authenticated certificate. The archive distinguishes mathematical event receipts from verification receipts that record a computational audit. See [[rsr]] and [[verification-receipt]].

terms.title: Registered distinction
terms.status: D
terms.section: II. Possibility, action, events, and historical registration
terms.body:
A registered distinction is a difference retained strongly enough to remain available to the declared history or comparison. The event-level notation is delta_e. Delta[Gamma] denotes a specified retained composition of distinctions along the history Gamma.

```text
realized transduction -> delta_e -> Delta[Gamma] -> chosen readout
```

The composition need not be a scalar sum, and neither delta_e nor Delta[Gamma] is automatically a duration. A scalar time rendering requires the separate winding construction; a measure requires its own weighting and readout.

The old heading "Delta" is retained as an indexed historical alias, not as a universal operator definition. Delta_1800 is a particular involution on a G1800 carrier; it is not delta_e or Delta[Gamma]. The projective address-return operator called H in another Sigma thread is also not identified with Delta by notation.

terms.title: Registration
terms.status: D
terms.section: II. Possibility, action, events, and historical registration
terms.body:
Registration is the admitted process by which a realized relational distinction is represented in a receipt, pointer, stable record, or history domain. It answers what was recorded as having happened. It is not automatically the upstream process that selected the event.

A faithful registration preserves the intended distinction or measure at the interface it is registering. A new operation that changes the measure, introduces new information, or changes the preparation is a different process and needs its own accounting. Registration can be physically interactive; calling it downstream does not mean it is causally inert.

The glossary separates event registration, finite frequency realization, and native source provenance. Their interaction must be demonstrated rather than hidden in the word "measurement." See [[registered-measure]], [[nonamplification]], and [[source-provenance]].

terms.title: Event primacy
terms.status: D/H; methodological principle
terms.section: II. Possibility, action, events, and historical registration
terms.body:
Event primacy is the QR principle that becoming is modeled through completed relational occurrences and their composition, while states represent conditions before, after, or across those occurrences. The compact formulation is "physical becoming is fundamentally event composition, not merely state succession."

This does not make state mathematics invalid. It demands that a succession of state labels be related to an admitted event grammar, complete output accounting, and registration before it is interpreted as becoming. Endpoint equality alone does not recover the order or receipts of the intervening events.

The word "physical" in the programmatic formulation remains a hypothesis about interpretation. The finite theorems concern particular event, history, and carrier constructions. An internal presentation orbit is not automatically a sequence of physical completed events, and a phase index is not automatically elapsed time.

terms.title: Becoming
terms.status: D
terms.section: II. Possibility, action, events, and historical registration
terms.body:
Becoming is the ordered composition of admitted realized relational events through which relational organization changes while complete informational accounting is preserved. In the propagation sector, one primitive occurrence is one completed receipted handoff.

```text
Gamma = E_n o ... o E_2 o E_1
```

The order matters. Histories with the same endpoint can differ in their retained receipts, orientation, or later admissible response. Becoming therefore is not defined merely as a scalar increase, a rise in complexity, or a count of unexplained updates.

Registered becoming supplies the history from which a Thalean-time readout can be defined. It need not presuppose an external clock in the finite formalism. This does not establish that every event advances the selected winding, nor that diminishing freedom defines time.

terms.title: Registered history
terms.status: D
terms.section: II. Possibility, action, events, and historical registration
terms.body:
Registered history is the ordered compositional record of realized relational events together with the retained distinctions that keep those occurrences accountable. "History = attested actuality" is its compact reading. It is richer than a list of visible endpoint configurations.

An extensible log acquires another occurrence when a new event is appended. This statement does not imply that every compressed history observable grows, that every event creates an independent degree, or that tau_Th increases at every step. The full word, a retained sufficient register, and a scalar history readout are different objects.

A passive archive is evidence about prior events. A history-dependent controller additionally reads retained distinctions and uses them in future admission or response. That extra coupling is needed before stored history explains a new branch selection. See [[predictive-history]] and [[history-bearing-transducer]].

terms.title: Law and relation before law
terms.status: D/H; program interpretation
terms.section: II. Possibility, action, events, and historical registration
terms.body:
In the QR framing, a law is a stable constraint or invariant of admissible relational composition. "Relation is primitive to law" means that the program starts with relations and asks what transformations they admit, rather than imagining an external command applied to otherwise independent objects.

Today's formulation, "law resides in permissible action," makes permission the explanatory target. It does not collapse the admission rule into an outcome-frequency table or make a record of what happened a complete source law. A probabilistic law can be mathematically represented where supplied; the QR hypothesis is that probability need not be the primitive instruction consulted by each event.

A useful law must specify its domain and survive the relevant compositional tests. Calling an observed pattern "law" does not establish uniqueness, native provenance, or a physical conservation principle beyond the evidence retained for that construction.

terms.title: Foreclosed alternative
terms.status: D; context-qualified interpretation
terms.section: II. Possibility, action, events, and historical registration
terms.body:
A foreclosed alternative is a continuation that was admitted at an earlier prefix but is no longer a compatible extension of the now-realized history in the same declared frame. This gives a precise reading of the discussion's claim that an unrealized alternative becomes impossible after an action: it becomes incompatible with that realized occurrence as its alternative past, not impossible in every future context.

An opportunity can survive even when its earlier ordering does not. Choosing one task now can foreclose the history "the other task first" while leaving the other task available later. Thus historical alternatives and carried-forward action capacity are not the same inventory.

Foreclosure should always name its comparison frame and horizon. It is not automatically information destruction, irreversibility of complete transduction, or a positive increment of Thalean time. See [[opportunity-cost]] and [[finite-frame-freedom]].

terms.title: Thalean conservation of information
terms.status: D/H as QR principle; P for declared recoverable maps
terms.section: III. Recoverability, memory, closure, and comparison
terms.body:
Thalean conservation of information says that admissible becoming may redistribute relational information between propagation and receipt but may not erase the distinction structure needed to reconstruct the completed event. Its primitive mathematical content is recoverability of the complete input from the complete admitted output.

The slogan "what propagates plus what is retained accounts for the event" is not an already-derived additive entropy equation. A scalar information functional would need its own definition and, where relevant, correlation terms. Information conservation does not imply that complexity, local freedom, every marginal, or every visible readout is numerically constant.

Today's keeper is "freedom can be spent; information cannot be discarded." Future choices can be restricted while the output still records the distinction needed to account for that restriction. This is a structural accounting requirement, not yet an identification with every standard physical conservation law.

terms.title: Recoverability
terms.status: D/P
terms.section: III. Recoverability, memory, closure, and comparison
terms.body:
Recoverability means that a reconstruction map returns the complete input from the complete output on the admitted image. In a finite classical model this is equivalent to injectivity of the complete transduction.

```text
Rec_e(T_e(z)) = z
```

Either output alone can be many-to-one. For example, the supplied bit illustration T(u,v)=(u+v,v), with addition modulo two, is recovered by (p,r)->(p+r,r). The first component alone loses a distinction; the pair does not. This illustrates reorganization, not copying an extra input bit into existence.

Recovery on an image does not imply every formal output pair is reachable, every inverse is an admitted forward experiment, or every history word can be physically erased. The source domain, retained memory, and permitted inverse operation must be specified.

terms.title: Complete input and complete microscopic description
terms.status: D
terms.section: III. Recoverability, memory, closure, and comparison
terms.body:
The complete input contains every variable whose distinction must survive the stated transduction, including prior local memory. If the operation is T_e(x,m)=(p,m'), retaining only enough information to recover x is insufficient when distinct prior memories m were also part of the admitted domain.

This complete accounting description differs from the [[operational-state]]. The latter can intentionally identify histories that no admitted future test distinguishes. Such a reduction is useful but must not be substituted into a microscopic recovery claim without saying which distinctions are being quotiented out.

The same distinction governs archives: a short glossary can be an excellent re-entry surface without being a lossless transcript. Its source ledger and preserved baseline make the compression accountable; they do not turn the glossary into the complete historical record.

terms.title: Receipt capacity
terms.status: P under a declared finite classical model
terms.section: III. Recoverability, memory, closure, and comparison
terms.body:
Receipt capacity is the amount of retained label space needed to make a prescribed propagated map recoverable. For a finite map p:X->Y completed by a receipt r:X->R, the pair (p,r) is injective exactly when r distinguishes every pair of inputs lying in the same p-fiber.

The manuscript's finite bound is:

```text
|R| >= max_y |p^-1(y)|
```

With freely assignable receipt labels this bound is attainable. It counts distinguishable labels, not a thermodynamic energy or an independently calibrated physical information unit. A bit count would require a chosen encoding and a ceiling logarithm.

This term sharpens "complementary receipt": the needed record is relative to what the propagated component forgets. When p is injective, one constant receipt label is enough for reconstruction, though an operational apparatus may retain more.

terms.title: Complete operational QR state
terms.status: D
terms.section: III. Recoverability, memory, closure, and comparison
terms.body:
The complete operational QR state is the present configuration together with retained distinctions relevant to future admitted response. Its completeness is relative to a declared apparatus, continuation language, and response family, not to every microscopic detail of the past.

A retained distinction matters when it changes which future tests are admitted or how an admitted test responds. Two equal visible endpoints can therefore be operationally different. Conversely an inaccessible detail not represented in any admitted future test need not be retained in the effective state description.

This is not a permission to destroy distinctions in a complete information-conserving transduction. It is a choice of reduced description. The full input/output accounting and the predictive quotient should be separately typed. See [[predictive-history]] and [[complete-input]].

terms.title: Predictive history equivalence
terms.status: D/P on a declared response language
terms.section: III. Recoverability, memory, closure, and comparison
terms.body:
Two histories are predictively equivalent when they have the same admitted future language and the same registered response to every test in that language. Both conditions are needed.

```text
h1 ~_pred h2 iff
  L(h1) = L(h2), and
  O(h1,w) = O(h2,w) for every w in that common language.
```

The baseline's wording in terms of "common future continuations" is tightened using the later manuscript. Equality only on the intersection of two different languages can be vacuous, even when one history permits actions the other forbids. That is not predictive equivalence.

A predictive class is a state-reduction tool. It does not imply that the full records are identical or that all forgotten information has been erased physically. Where the continuation grammar is closed under common extension, the equivalence must remain compatible with that extension.

terms.title: Memory
terms.status: D
terms.section: III. Recoverability, memory, closure, and comparison
terms.body:
Memory is retained distinction with future discriminating power in a specified transducer or apparatus. The test is operational: some future admission decision or response can depend on the distinction under a controlled comparison.

A receipt can exist as historical evidence without the next operation reading it. Conversely a compact retained register can preserve exactly the distinctions needed for future response without storing a verbatim transcript. Memory, receipt, archive, and complete history are therefore related but not interchangeable.

The physical interpretation of a particular memory carrier needs an implementation. The finite definition neither imports consciousness nor assigns arbitrary inaccessible past details to physical state. It supplies the criterion used when deciding whether an alleged hidden history actually does explanatory work in the model.

terms.title: Visible return and complete return
terms.status: D/P on stated projections
terms.section: III. Recoverability, memory, closure, and comparison
terms.body:
Visible return occurs when a chosen projected or reduced configuration returns to a previous value. Complete return requires recurrence of the complete state on the declared carrier. They are not equivalent when a projection forgets lift or retained-register information.

The registered five-frame example distinguishes q(F^10 x)=q(x) from F^10 x=x: the G900 receipt can repeat while the G1800 lift differs. Full carrier recurrence at F^20 still does not make an append-only history word empty; a new traversal has occurred even if the finite state recurs.

Thus three levels must be named: projected-state return, complete finite-carrier return, and equality of an ordered historical record. The baseline's phrase "history returns" must always specify a compressed history state or equivalence, rather than imply that chronology has automatically been undone.

terms.title: Closure
terms.status: D; operation-specific C/H
terms.section: III. Recoverability, memory, closure, and comparison
terms.body:
Closure is an admitted operation bringing relational histories or presentations into a common comparison context so that a distinction can be registered or tested. It need not erase the difference between the compared histories or restore their complete initial state.

A graph cycle, a quotient return, an episode closure, and a comparison closure can all participate in the program, but each has its own domain and criterion. A closed quotient path can retain nontrivial holonomy upstairs. A completed comparison can leave a residue that matters later.

The term does not assert that every thalion autonomously seeks closure. That would require a source or feedback law. Preserve the separation "closure != complete historical return" and distinguish the closure operation from its retained [[closure-residue]].

terms.title: Closure residue
terms.status: D
terms.section: III. Recoverability, memory, closure, and comparison
terms.body:
A closure residue is the retained relational distinction that survives an admitted closure or comparison. It records what remains different after the histories have been brought into the required common context.

Its type can be a group element, parity, phase, vector, register value, or another specified object. No universal scalar or common central element is assigned to every residue. A residue contributes to a receipt when that retained content is part of the completed-event accounting.

The phrase "history enters rich; closure leaves a residue" describes a compression, not automatic destruction of the rest of the complete information. Whether the residue affects the future is the separate [[closure-feedback]] test. Whether it is spin-sensitive is the narrower [[rsr]] question.

terms.title: Closure feedback
terms.status: D; H until a specific dependence is supplied
terms.section: III. Recoverability, memory, closure, and comparison
terms.body:
Closure feedback is a dependence of a later admitted continuation or registered response on a residue retained from an earlier closure. Writing Adm_(n+1)=Adm_(n+1)(r_n) names the proposed dependence; it does not prove it.

A witness must compare different r_n values while holding the other relevant context fixed. The residue might change permission, a branch designation, or the response to a common future test. Those mechanisms should be reported separately rather than compressed into the assertion that history "must" select the next event.

The existence of a residue, a storage register, or a nontrivial group commutator alone does not establish feedback. The current program contains candidate and scoped coupling examples, not a universal law that every retained distinction is read by every later event.

terms.title: Sigma
terms.status: D; particular operators require carrier-specific definitions
terms.section: III. Recoverability, memory, closure, and comparison
terms.body:
Sigma denotes a relational comparison or encounter operation/interface in the program. It identifies the operation through which relational distinctions meet, are compared, or become exposed to registration.

Sigma is not the residue produced by the encounter. In particular Sigma != RSR. Nor is the use of Sigma a promise that every comparison can be represented by one universal matrix across G60, G1800, the history carrier, and a physical apparatus.

When a branch uses Sigma for a more specific state-action construction, preserve its domain, quotient, and operator definitions. The native Delta_1800 transport and the external address-return/survival operator H must not be identified merely because both appeared in Sigma work. This glossary retains that non-identification without reopening their separate audits.

terms.title: Relational Spin Residue (RSR)
terms.status: D/C; F for physical spin correspondence
terms.section: III. Recoverability, memory, closure, and comparison
terms.body:
Relational Spin Residue is the name reserved for a specifically established spin-related central or projective residue retained by an oriented relational composition. The compact phrase is "the spin-sensitive difference that survives relational closure."

It is narrower than a generic trace, receipt, or holonomy. To use the name rigorously, identify the lifted action, the projection that hides the distinction, the retained element or register, and the algebra making the distinction spin-related in that construction. A nontrivial finite parity is not automatically physical spin.

The physical embedding remains separate: the existence of a central minus sign, order-four parent, or real complex structure does not alone identify electron spin, a laboratory qubit, or hbar. Sigma names the encounter; RSR names a specialized retained consequence.

terms.title: Local sufficiency and decoding
terms.status: D/P on a declared readout
terms.section: III. Recoverability, memory, closure, and comparison
terms.body:
A local interface is sufficient for a desired readout when that readout is constant on every fiber of the data available at the interface. Equivalently, a decoder exists from the available local data to the intended output.

This is the archive's criterion for saying that a transducer "relays" a scalar or a relational distinction. If two complete states look identical to the interface but require different decoded values, no decoder using only that interface can succeed. A new source of information or an enriched retained register would be required.

For incremental scalar accounting, absolute reconstruction also needs a reference value. Correct increments do not determine an unknown starting level. The criterion separates exact reconstructibility from visual resemblance, statistical correlation, and a convenient coordinate formula. See [[scalar-relay]].

terms.title: Transport cocycle
terms.status: D/C on a specified coefficient system
terms.section: III. Recoverability, memory, closure, and comparison
terms.body:
A transport cocycle assigns compositional displacement or residue to admitted histories. In the scalar additive case used in the baseline:

```text
Xi(gamma2 o gamma1) = Xi(gamma2) + Xi(gamma1)
```

A positive execution cost can also add, giving a ratio Xi(gamma)/Cost(gamma) when its domain and units are declared. This does not automatically equal c_Th, which uses field distance and irreducible event depth.

For frame-dependent quantities the second contribution may need transport into the first frame. The retained G9000 readout uses a law of the form d(t+s)=d(t)+T^t d(s). That is not the same as an untwisted scalar sum. Likewise the analyzer multiplication factor omega(g,h) is a two-cocycle, not an additive path displacement. Shared terminology does not identify these objects.

terms.title: Informative coupling
terms.status: D; finite witnesses have their own scope
terms.section: IV. Dependence, current, conservation, and backaction
terms.body:
A law is informatively coupled to a retained distinction r beyond other variables s when changing r, while fixing the declared context z and s, changes an admitted continuation set or a registered response to a common admitted test.

```text
Adm(z,r,s) != Adm(z,r',s)
  or
O_(z,r,s)(w) != O_(z,r',s)(w)
```

A stochastic comparison uses response distributions under the same declared intervention and preparation conditions. This is operational dependence, not mere coexistence of labels or an observed correlation.

Coupling can remain entirely local. An actual [[information-current]] additionally transports a distinguishable payload through admitted handoffs to a decoder. An extra cover coordinate is therefore not informative just because it exists; a dependence on that coordinate must be demonstrated.

terms.title: Information current
terms.status: D; F for a physical flux identification
terms.section: IV. Dependence, current, conservation, and backaction
terms.body:
An information current is transport of an operationally distinguishable payload through admitted field handoffs, with a specified encoding, continuation law, and downstream decoding. Each participating handoff must preserve a relevant downstream dependence on the incoming distinction within the complete-output accounting.

An actual current uses informative coupling. The converse fails: a local comparison can depend on a retained variable without transmitting it to a new address. A static correlation, nonzero parity, or a stored receipt is not by itself a current.

Quantitative flux would additionally require a measure, interface, and event or time normalization. The spectral operator D5 is called a five-frame difference current in a separate algebraic sense; that name does not independently provide a physical signal, electric current, energy flux, or decoded payload. See [[frame-current]].

terms.title: Conservative informative action
terms.status: D/C for a supplied invariant
terms.section: IV. Dependence, current, conservation, and backaction
terms.body:
A conservative informative action is an already-admitted, recoverable, informative transduction that preserves an additional specified invariant I_inv on its admitted complete-state domain.

```text
I_inv(T_e z) = I_inv(z)
```

Recovery, informativeness, and conservation of the chosen invariant are three separate tests. An invariant scalar can be preserved by a many-to-one map; that does not establish complete recovery. A reversible map can leave a particular readout unchanged without being informative for that readout family.

The invariant need not be relational complexity. A useful supplied linear model has I_G(X)=X^dagger G_metric X for a fixed positive Hermitian form. Such comparison models illustrate conserved content under changing organization; they do not prove that all QR action is linear, norm-preserving, or an adjacent transmission.

terms.title: Invariant and positive Hermitian form
terms.status: D/C
terms.section: IV. Dependence, current, conservation, and backaction
terms.body:
An invariant is a declared readout unchanged by the specified admitted action. In the conservative linear comparison, G_metric is a fixed positive-definite Hermitian form and I_G(X)=X^dagger G_metric X is the associated quadratic invariant candidate.

The representation and its relation to registered distinctions must be given before calling the form "informational." Merely writing a positive quadratic expression does not make it conserved, make it informationally complete, or identify it with C(R).

The notation must remain separate from G_base in the scalar encoding, G60 and other graph names, G_hist in the history Gram construction, and G_plus in the analyzer Gram kernel. Different positive forms or normalizations can describe different comparison problems; they are not interchangeable units by default.

terms.title: Represented generator and propagator
terms.status: D/C in specified comparison models
terms.section: IV. Dependence, current, conservation, and backaction
terms.body:
A represented generator A_lin specifies infinitesimal evolution in an admitted linear model; a propagator U_lin implements the corresponding finite update. These are represented operations, not automatically source-derived generators of the native graph.

For a fixed positive Hermitian form, the retained conservative criterion is:

```text
A_lin^dagger G_metric + G_metric A_lin = 0
```

Under the stated linear evolution, this preserves X^dagger G_metric X. The criterion does not select A_lin uniquely, prove graph locality, supply an instrument, or identify the evolution parameter with physical time.

The gyro and Maxwell examples are comparison models with their own inputs. Their successful algebra must not be relabeled as a native WXYZTI, Thalion, or history-sector dynamics without a common-domain construction. See [[comparison-models]].

terms.title: Informative backaction
terms.status: D; C reported in retrieved conversation; native Born actor remains open
terms.section: IV. Dependence, current, conservation, and backaction
terms.body:
Informative backaction is an action-induced change in retained relational state that can affect a subsequent admitted continuation or registered response. It is stronger than simply noting that a measurement or encounter occurred, because the retained change must have an operational consequence.

Today's original double-slit thread reports a pair-envelope example with genuine backaction: the same relative control can produce different macro-actions for different retained pair relations. This provides a scoped dependence witness, not a completed Born-selection law.

The retrieved discussion explicitly distinguishes that example from the desired history-sector event actor Y_(ij)=-C_ij J_hist. The source-ordered event mechanism, its connection to the Born spectral sector, and the relative-control schedule remain open. The archive preserves the finding without turning the word "backaction" into a universal quantum measurement postulate.

terms.title: Retained pair relation and relative-control actuator
terms.status: C as conversation-reported formula; source schedule H
terms.section: IV. Dependence, current, conservation, and backaction
terms.body:
In the retrieved pair-envelope discussion, R_pair=pq denotes the retained relation between the two pair variables, and d_ctrl=g h^-1 denotes the relative control. The reported actuator law is:

```text
c_n = a^(mu(d_ctrl,n)) R_pair,n
c_n = 1 -> T10
c_n = a -> T12
```

The notation is local to that construction. The binary exponent convention mu here is not silently identified with the +/-1-valued registered-event Mode. Nor are R_pair and the two outcome values assumed to range over a larger set than the source demonstrated.

The point is dependence: fixing the control while changing retained R_pair can change the action. The retrieved source does not supply the full variable domains, native chronological schedule, or an event-by-event Born crosswalk. This entry is an indexed research definition and reported formula, not an executable specification of the missing source law.

terms.title: Pair envelope and history-sector actor
terms.status: D/C reported; H for the required native coupling
terms.section: IV. Dependence, current, conservation, and backaction
terms.body:
The pair envelope is the retained two-part relational domain used in the backaction exploration. It supplies a place to test whether a prior pair distinction can influence subsequent action. The retrieved record establishes the term's role, not a complete independently replayable state inventory.

The Born-relevant target is instead an event actor whose product readout follows the history golden sector:

```text
Y_(ij) = -C_ij J_hist
```

The relation separates the context sign C_ij from the history-sector involution J_hist. The pair-envelope example was explicitly not promoted to that actor: the tested EPR controls made the relevant relative-orientation parity trivial.

This distinction preserves a useful positive result without overstating it. Informative backaction can be genuine while the specific source-to-Born connection remains absent. The 9,000-state ceiling constrains this search but does not solve the actor problem by spare capacity alone.

terms.title: Relational complexity
terms.status: D/H; universal native functional open
terms.section: V. Relational complexity, scalar readout, and orthogonality
terms.body:
Relational complexity is the proposed quantity measuring how much relational organization is present in a specified registered object. Write C(R) only after declaring the object domain, its registration level, the equivalence of presentations, and the functional being evaluated.

The source's compact phrase is "relational complexity of the thing." Its intended invariance is presentation-level: equivalent registered descriptions should not change the value. That does not imply C is preserved by every real transduction; organization can change while complete information remains recoverable.

A raw vertex count, return depth, event count, spectral rank, phase, or freedom measure is not the universal definition. The sketch's suggestion that x counts vertices in R_x was subsequently restricted: return depth or counting can be a special realization, but the universal native complexity functional remains open. See [[scalar-encoding]] and [[freedom]].

terms.title: Scalar encoding of relational complexity
terms.status: D/C once C and its base are supplied
terms.section: V. Relational complexity, scalar readout, and orthogonality
terms.body:
The optional scalar encoding is S_enc(R)=G_base^C(R), where G_base>1 is fixed and dimensionless. It renders a complexity value multiplicatively; it is not itself the definition of relational complexity.

```text
S_enc(R) = G_base^C(R)
C(R) = log_(G_base)(S_enc(R))
```

Changing the base changes the encoding, not the relational object. Two distinct objects with the same C can have the same encoded scalar. The scalar therefore need not be a complete state description, and its existence does not supply a local decoder or a physical unit.

The superscript x in the motivating G^x sketch is not locked to a universal vertex count. Use C(R), and identify any count-based special case explicitly. G_base is neither a graph G_n, Newton's constant, nor the Hermitian form G_metric.

terms.title: Scalar relay and local complexity increment
terms.status: D/C; local sufficiency required
terms.section: V. Relational complexity, scalar readout, and orthogonality
terms.body:
Scalar relay is continuity of relational accounting through a transduction, not movement of an independent scalar substance. A downstream interface reconstructs or updates the scalar from the relation and retained information available to it.

For a supplied functional and sufficient interface, the retained update is:

```text
C_(i+1) = C_i + Delta_C_i
S_(i+1) = S_i * G_base^(Delta_C_i)
```

The increments telescope across composition, but the absolute scalar requires an initial reference value. When the interface cannot distinguish inputs needing different increments, no local decoder of that increment exists without more information.

This is why "the transducer relays the scalar" must be interpreted carefully: it can propagate the information sufficient to regenerate a readout. It does not imply that C is energy, that scalar conservation replaces recoverability, or that every native event changes C by one.

terms.title: Orthogonality
terms.status: D/C; form or relation must be stated
terms.section: V. Relational complexity, scalar readout, and orthogonality
terms.body:
In the motivating shape discussion, the user explicitly assigned the vertical bar "|" the meaning orthogonality. In a linear realization, orthogonality means vanishing pairing under a specified inner product or bilinear form. In a diagram, it is a declared relation that still needs its mathematical carrier identified.

The symbol does not, by itself, prove a Euclidean spatial axis, a tensor factorization, causal independence, or lack of informative coupling. Orthogonal states can be connected by an admitted operation; an orthogonal decomposition can still participate in a correlated joint readout.

For the glossary, record which vectors, subspaces, or roles are orthogonal and under which form. A figure's visual right angle is not a native theorem unless the supporting relation has been reconstructed. This keeps the sketch useful without making its geometry an undeclared physical axiom.

terms.title: Null Well
terms.status: D/H; construction-specific rather than a universal operator
terms.section: V. Relational complexity, scalar readout, and orthogonality
terms.body:
Null Well is the project name used for a reference/comparison configuration in which a central null or non-traversable feature organizes the surrounding relation. The September sketch discussion places that feature centrally and uses orthogonality as a declared part of the picture.

The retrieved discussion distinguishes a period-two scaled recurrence in the Null Well analysis from the registered-event C3 phase. It does not establish that the sketch, the older apparatus orientation mode, and the new G9000 zero-current subspace are literally one object.

In the Scope apparatus framing, locked orientation includes the code, device, screen, embodied user, and readout chain. That is ordinary apparatus coordination, not a claim of quantum entanglement. Neither a visual null nor a zero-current mode means absence of all relational information. Use the source construction whenever the name is promoted beyond this glossary role.

terms.title: Selected reference
terms.status: D
terms.section: VI. References, incidence, orientation, Phase, and Mode
terms.body:
A selected reference is a declared datum used to coordinatize a presentation, comparison, or execution. It can label one member of a torsor positive, choose a local origin, or fix a frame convention. It supplies a readable account without making that datum physically privileged.

The adopted formulation is: "GR says no frame is privileged. QR says: agreed. Select one. Then we can start." This is the author's methodological statement, not a quotation of a relativistic theorem or a derivation of general covariance.

Reference selection cannot manufacture an incidence, alter an incompatible transport law, supply missing payload information, or make a nonunique source law unique. Distinguish passive reference choice from an apparatus change that genuinely alters the admitted interaction. See [[executing-reference]] and [[reconciliation]].

terms.title: Executing reference
terms.status: D
terms.section: VI. References, incidence, orientation, Phase, and Mode
terms.body:
An executing reference is a selected presentation at a declared registration interface, with retained local context and any orientation data required by its intended readout. It is where the account is operationally situated.

A selected label alone is not enough: the interface and available record determine what can actually be compared or decoded. An executor may have a definite local history without that history becoming an absolute frame for all other accounts. Another reference can support another situated presentation of the same relation.

This term is not the G9000 frame-common harmonic mode. The latter is an invariant subspace constant across frame labels; an executing reference is a presentation/interface datum. Calling both "reference" does not establish an identification between a person, an apparatus, and a 1,800-dimensional subspace.

terms.title: Reference signing and "I am 1"
terms.status: D
terms.section: VI. References, incidence, orientation, Phase, and Mode
terms.body:
Reference signing labels a two-member orientation torsor after selecting one member t_star. Its defining normalization is sigma_(t_star)(t_star)=+1, with the exchanged member assigned -1.

"I am 1" is the situated shorthand for that positive naming. It is not an identity between the executor and a number, the identity operator, one unit of relational complexity, one tick, or c_Th=1. The latter normalizations refer to different domains.

Changing the selected torsor member reverses both local signs. Relative comparison can remain unchanged when the objects and comparison data are transformed together. This is the limited, precise sense in which the positive name is conventional while the distinction between the two members remains real in the construction.

terms.title: Situated or subjective account
terms.status: D
terms.section: VI. References, incidence, orientation, Phase, and Mode
terms.body:
A situated account is a record and readout indexed to an executing reference. "Subjective" has this operational meaning in the QR reference discussion: the account is expressed from somewhere, using particular retained data and presentation conventions.

It does not mean inaccurate, unsigned, merely imagined, or physically privileged. Nor does the term require a theory of consciousness. The physics glossary deliberately uses registration and comparison language rather than importing unrelated claims about mental experience.

A situated account becomes objectively comparable when a declared map reconciles its represented objects, references, and readouts with another account. Agreement is a property of that comparison and its covariance, not the disappearance of all local perspectives. See [[reference-independent]].

terms.title: Reference-independent statement
terms.status: D/C on a stated transformation family
terms.section: VI. References, incidence, orientation, Phase, and Mode
terms.body:
A reference-independent statement is unchanged by the declared simultaneous transformation of its represented objects, reference data, and comparison laws. The domain and allowed transformations must be specified.

This is not a claim that every coordinate-dependent quantity is meaningless. Local signs, phase coordinates, and matrix entries can change while invariant products or corresponding readouts agree. Conversely numerical agreement in one chart does not establish a covariant law.

The term also does not assert unrestricted physical frame symmetry. A finite presentation action and the Lorentz or general-relativistic transformation problem are separate. The glossary uses covariance to specify what a comparison preserves, while reserving physical correspondence for a independently supported apparatus or continuum model.

terms.title: Incidence and incidence presentation
terms.status: D
terms.section: VI. References, incidence, orientation, Phase, and Mode
terms.body:
An incidence is the actual intermediate relation through which separately defined objects or presentations meet. An incidence presentation records the object together with that relation, for example (u,B) with u in B, rather than pretending the object alone carries every boundary sign.

Different incidences can give the same underlying state opposite signed boundary presentations without contradiction. Extra phase or endpoint data must be included explicitly when the intended readout needs them. Bare membership is not automatically a complete phase-decorated presentation.

"No path without incidence" is a useful mnemonic, but the theorem-bearing object is the specified relation and its maps. Equal dimensions, matching counts, or isomorphic abstract groups do not construct it. The history/analyzer program needs a common domain with projections to both registers, not just a shared appearance of the number twelve or 120.

terms.title: Signed incidence
terms.status: D/P on the declared cycle and interface domains
terms.section: VI. References, incidence, orientation, Phase, and Mode
terms.body:
Signed incidence is an incidence relation equipped with orientation comparison coefficients. For an oriented cycle and an oriented edge, the coefficient records agreement, disagreement, or non-incidence. The signed cycle matrix B_hist is one concrete example.

Under edge and history reference changes:

```text
B' = D_E B D_H
(B')^T B' = D_H B^T B D_H
```

The arbitrary edge signs cancel from the Gram. Relative overlap survives while its presentation in the history basis changes covariantly. A signed action must also satisfy the appropriate intertwining equation, such as U_E(g) B = B U_H(g).

An unsigned action can fail even when it permutes the same underlying cycles correctly. This is why a set-level identification and an oriented vector-space intertwiner are separate accomplishments, and why signs cannot be reconstructed solely from a common incidence count.

terms.title: Orientation torsor
terms.status: D
terms.section: VI. References, incidence, orientation, Phase, and Mode
terms.body:
An orientation torsor is a two-member set with a free transitive C2 action and no intrinsically preferred positive member. The structure determines an exchange and a relative distinction before any reference supplies +/- names.

A selected member provides coordinates; it does not create the pair. An equivariant global choice can be obstructed when an allowed symmetry exchanges both members while fixing the base datum. In such a case the unordered pair can be canonical even though no canonical representative exists.

This language applies to several separately constructed orientation pairs. It does not identify them automatically. A b/ab designation torsor, an inverse-current pair, a signed analyzer convention, and a local reference torsor require an actual comparison map before they can be used as one bit.

terms.title: Isotropy and stabilizer
terms.status: D
terms.section: VI. References, incidence, orientation, Phase, and Mode
terms.body:
The isotropy subgroup of a point or incidence consists of transformations fixing that chosen datum. It describes residual freedom in presentation after the base datum has been fixed.

For orientation reconciliation, the action of isotropy on the two sign fibers is decisive. If the two endpoint sign characters disagree on a stabilizer element, transport around the fixed base cannot give a consistent comparison. Naming a positive reference does not repair that mismatch.

A graph-position stabilizer, a face stabilizer, a cycle stabilizer, and the isotropy of a history groupoid act on different domains. Their orders and abstract group names are not interchangeable. This term is used to state a concrete compatibility test, not to infer one from a coincident count such as eight, sixteen, or eighty.

terms.title: Section and equivariant section
terms.status: D/P on a specified projection
terms.section: VI. References, incidence, orientation, Phase, and Mode
terms.body:
A section chooses one preimage over each base point of a projection. An equivariant section makes that choice commute with the declared group action.

A reference can choose a member locally without establishing an equivariant global choice. In a finite G-set formulation, a section exists equivariantly only when each representative fiber contains a point fixed by the stabilizer of its base point. This is the structural source of several no-canonical-sign statements in the program.

An arbitrary signed representative or coordinate convention can still be useful. The archive records it as a supplied section, not as a native invariant selection. A failed section does not imply that no equivariant relation between two unpointed torsors can exist; simultaneous reversal can remain compatible with a comparison.

terms.title: Common action domain
terms.status: D; construction-specific X/H
terms.section: VI. References, incidence, orientation, Phase, and Mode
terms.body:
A common action domain is a specified carrier of incidences or coupled states equipped with projections to the objects being compared and an action compatible with both projections. It makes the proposed relation between two registers testable on the same inputs.

A shared dimension, spectrum, or abstract group is insufficient. The required data include the actual incidences, endpoint projections, allowed actors, lifted signs or phases, and any readout map. The orbit structure matters because independent orbits can retain independent comparison choices.

The latest conversation reports such a domain for the twelve pentagons and two sheets times six analyzer axes. That particular claim is archived separately from the general definition and from the still-open G9000 frame-current map. See [[history-axis-domain]] and [[frame-history-intertwiner]].

terms.title: Orientation reconciliation criterion
terms.status: P/C on supplied honest cocycle actions
terms.section: VI. References, incidence, orientation, Phase, and Mode
terms.body:
Orientation reconciliation is a covariant comparison of two sign torsors over an admitted incidence. If the local sign actions are c_A(g,xi) and c_H(g,xi), a comparison coefficient kappa must satisfy:

```text
kappa(g xi) c_H(g,xi) = c_A(g,xi) kappa(xi)
```

On a nonempty transitive incidence domain with honest C2 cocycles, such a comparison exists exactly when the two sign characters agree on every element of the isotropy subgroup at one incidence. If it exists, there are two choices, differing by one overall sign. With N separately compatible orbits there are 2^N choices.

This theorem is conditional on the common domain and actual lifted actions. It neither guarantees that a proposed native pair has those data nor turns every orientation problem into "one missing global bit." The bit count follows only after the orbit and isotropy checks.

terms.title: Sign cocycle and projective factor set
terms.status: D; concrete laws source-specific
terms.section: VI. References, incidence, orientation, Phase, and Mode
terms.body:
A sign cocycle describes how a signed fiber transforms consistently under composition. For a sign action over incidences, c(gh,xi)=c(g,h xi)c(h,xi). A projective representation instead has a multiplication factor omega(g,h) defined by M_g M_h=omega(g,h)M_(gh).

The two formulas address different levels: transport of a sign over a base action, and a central defect in multiplication of chosen operator representatives. Their consistency requirements follow from composition, but they must not be conflated with an additive path displacement Xi.

A change of signs in the chosen section can change the representative factor set. The particular formula omega=(-1)^(p(g)p(h)) reported in the latest history chart belongs to that chart; it is not a universal cocycle for every signed-axis presentation in the project.

terms.title: Switching covariance
terms.status: D/P on the supplied analyzer tables
terms.section: VI. References, incidence, orientation, Phase, and Mode
terms.body:
Switching covariance is consistency under changes of signed axis representatives accompanied by the corresponding outcome relabeling. For a chosen analyzer chart:

```text
n_i -> d_i n_i
C_ij -> d_i d_j C_ij
a -> d_i a,  b -> d_j b
```

The product a b C_ij is unchanged. A joint table depending on this product can therefore be well defined modulo local sign conventions even when an unoriented line does not choose a signed observable.

A passive relabeling leaves the represented spectral effect unchanged. Changing an actual apparatus observable while holding the labels fixed is a different operation requiring an admitted instrument. This distinction preserves the orientation obstruction without needlessly requiring a privileged global sign for the statistical table.

terms.title: Global reversal
terms.status: D; carrier-specific action required
terms.section: VI. References, incidence, orientation, Phase, and Mode
terms.body:
Global reversal is a simultaneous exchange of the relevant sign conventions or members across a connected compatible domain. In a two-outcome joint readout, (a,b)->(-a,-b) preserves product parity while exchanging the two individual cells inside each parity class.

The term must name its object. Reversing vector representatives, exchanging receipt sheets, changing a current orientation, and acting by the central spinor matrix -I2 need not be the same operation. In particular conjugation by -I2 leaves observables unchanged; it is not automatically reversal of a physical analyzer vector.

Exactly two globally related comparisons are justified by a transitive compatible domain, not by the mere existence of two labels. Separate orbits can carry more than one independent sign, and incompatible isotropy can prevent any comparison.

terms.title: Projective action and linearization
terms.status: D
terms.section: VI. References, incidence, orientation, Phase, and Mode
terms.body:
A projective action is represented by operators whose products agree with the represented group product only up to a central scalar factor. In the current signed setting the factor is +/-1.

```text
M_g M_h = omega(g,h) M_(gh)
```

This is a coherent representation structure when the factor set obeys the required cocycle identity. It is not an error simply because the operators do not form an ordinary representation in the chosen section.

Linearization supplies an enlarged representation or additional factor whose multiplication compensates the defect. The latest history discussion reports a receipt-sheet factor doing exactly this for the signed six-axis action. That is a specific construction claim, not a theorem that every projective effect is missing historical memory. See [[history-linearization]].

terms.title: Phase and registered event phase
terms.status: D/C; carrier-typed
terms.section: VI. References, incidence, orientation, Phase, and Mode
terms.body:
Phase is position within a declared cyclic, harmonic, or registered presentation structure. In the specific registered-event S3 frame construction, Phase is the C3 coordinate p in C_evt^p M_evt^m f_star, with p in Z3.

```text
C_evt : (p,m) -> (p+1,m)
M_evt : (p,m) -> (-p,1-m)
```

This is a semidirect action, not two commuting independent dynamics. The event phase is not the same coordinate as a C5 character, the registered C20 phase, an axial rotor phase, or a physical oscillation angle. Each requires its own carrier and normalization.

A phase coordinate can distinguish presentations while leaving an event-type invariant unchanged. It does not identify distinct completed occurrences or supply a duration. See [[mode]], [[event-frame]], and [[recurrence-frequency]].

terms.title: Mode
terms.status: D; P/C on the supplied free frame action
terms.section: VI. References, incidence, orientation, Phase, and Mode
terms.body:
Mode is the S3 orientation parity of the registered event cycle. On the declared free frame orbit, choose one reference presentation f_star and define mu(g f_star)=sgn(g), with values +1 and -1. The two orientation classes are intrinsic; the reference fixes which one is named positive.

The phase generator C_evt has order three, and the register-reversing reflection M_evt has order two. They obey M_evt C_evt M_evt=C_evt^-1. Mode is therefore not a scalar amount, an eigenmode, a binary reduction of Thalean time, or a probability.

The state class and the actor are different: b/ab or another verified orientation pair supplies states, while M_evt is an operation exchanging classes. This S3 belongs to the registered-event frame construction, not to a claimed full S3 conjugation action on the native V4 elements.

terms.title: Registered event frame and event-presentation invariant
terms.status: D/P on the specified S3 model
terms.section: VI. References, incidence, orientation, Phase, and Mode
terms.body:
The registered relative closure-frame set consists of ordered distinct transpositions (r_close,rho_res) in S3. Their relative product q_rel=r_close^-1 rho_res is one of the two inverse three-cycles. The supplied native orientation work interprets the two entries as closing reflection and residue.

The six frames form a free transitive conjugation orbit. A frame has unique coordinates C_evt^p M_evt^m f_star. The event-presentation invariant is the declared event type or relational structure retained across this presentation action.

Neither frame entry alone determines the relative product over the full orbit. Nor does preservation of an event type identify two completed occurrences as one event. The frame's six presentations, the four Born outcome cells, and the twelve pentagon coefficient directions are different carriers despite sharing small factors.

terms.title: Collective eigenmode
terms.status: D/C for a supplied update operator
terms.section: VI. References, incidence, orientation, Phase, and Mode
terms.body:
A collective eigenmode is an eigenvector or invariant subspace of a specified global linear update. It describes how a represented field or carrier transforms under that update. It is not capital-M Mode, the registered-event orientation parity.

For a unitary realization, an eigenvalue has unit modulus and its argument supplies a represented phase increment. Reduced descriptions can exhibit contraction when complementary outputs are omitted, but the corresponding complete-output accounting must remain explicit.

An eigenmode is not automatically a particle, thermal state, or physically propagating wave. Those interpretations require preparation, stability, transport, interaction, and readout correspondences. In balanced-release formulas, "outgoing field modes" means such admitted eigenmodes, not the two S3 orientation classes.

terms.title: Event orientation under transport
terms.status: D/H; tested relation is carrier-specific
terms.section: VI. References, incidence, orientation, Phase, and Mode
terms.body:
Event orientation describes whether a specified carrier map preserves or reverses a declared local event structure. For event operators E_s and E_t and carrier map C_ts, the candidate test is:
