```text
C_ts E_s = sigma_ts E_t C_ts
sigma_ts in {+1,-1}
```

The plus sign means preservation in this representation; the minus sign means reversal. If neither relation holds, the map does not preserve the tested structure in either of those two senses.

This is not a universal primitive QR axiom, and it does not make determinant parity, deck sign, analyzer sign, or physical orientation the same character. The Program-4 comparisons retain separate status for each actor and domain. See [[defect-transport]].

terms.title: Sheet
terms.status: D; specialized sheets retain distinct domains
terms.section: VI. References, incidence, orientation, Phase, and Mode
terms.body:
A sheet is a distinguished component or presentation in a declared cover, registration, spectral decomposition, or history construction. The name describes a role, not one universal kind of object.

A deck sheet is a lift coordinate; a b/ab history sheet is a six-pentagon receipt family; a spectral sheet is an invariant subspace; a registered-event Mode sheet is one three-element orientation class. None is automatically a physical membrane or extra spatial dimension.

When two sheets are compared, state whether an operation exchanges their basis states, changes a grading, flips a spectral eigenvalue, or merely changes labels. These are different acts. The history grading Z_hist and the charted sheet-exchange Q_H provide a concrete example of distinct operators associated with the same two-sheet organization.

terms.title: Defect transport and orientation covariance
terms.status: C/P as reported in Program-4 checkpoints; broader covariance open
terms.section: VI. References, incidence, orientation, Phase, and Mode
terms.body:
The retained Program-4 defect-transport core is a comparison grammar: an actor preserves a canonically identified boundary/support and a relational invariant while moving the directed registration. Its common form is B_i(h_i x) identified with B_i(x), pi_i(h_i x) != pi_i(x), and I_i(h_i x)=I_i(x).

The standing checkpoint reports this core in all three programs. The stronger orientation-covariance claim was supported in Programs 2 and 3 but not Program 1, where the required transported T sign was not derived. Eight facewise sign choices and two uniform choices in the later discussion do not themselves prove one global character.

The term belongs to finite comparison anatomy. It is not a derivation of special relativity, a physical rod defect, observer transformations, or a universal conjugation law. The glossary retains the stronger and weaker statements separately.

terms.title: Event step, primitive depth, and macro-event
terms.status: D; grammar-dependent
terms.section: VII. Event depth, field reach, time, and recurrence
terms.body:
An event step is an irreducible operation in the specified admitted event grammar. In the causal propagation sector it is the primitive local handoff unit. Event depth |gamma|_event is the nonnegative number of such primitive steps needed for the declared history or operation.

A macro-event is a named composite. Renaming a long process as one macro does not reduce its primitive depth or increase its causal slope. Internal conservative updates are not automatically adjacent handoffs; the source must say whether and how they contribute to the denominator used in a propagation calculation.

Depth is distinct from oriented winding, recurrence period, and a physical clock duration. The original baseline's repeated step definitions are consolidated here, with the later zero-displacement/internal-operation qualification retained explicitly. See [[thalean-c]] and [[thalean-tick]].

terms.title: Event-preserving history
terms.status: D
terms.section: VII. Event depth, field reach, time, and recurrence
terms.body:
An event-preserving history is an admitted composition that keeps the declared relational distinction being propagated identifiable through its transductions and carrier handoffs. It includes the complementary accounting needed for reconstruction at the stated level.

This is stronger than observing that some disturbance travels. The encoded distinction, the transfer maps, and the eventual decoder must remain compatible. Apparent continuity of a plotted signal does not establish identity of the transported payload.

Such histories form the domain of the causal-slope definition. Their admissibility is not inferred from a desired speed or a chosen endpoint distance. The distinction can change presentation or orientation under a known transport law while remaining the same accountable payload in the declared representation.

terms.title: Field address and field distance
terms.status: D/C on a declared transducer network
terms.section: VII. Event depth, field reach, time, and recurrence
terms.body:
A field address locates a transducer or interface in the declared relational network. Field distance d_field is the admitted distance between such addresses, typically counted in neighboring handoffs under the specified locality rule.

It is not automatically Euclidean length, physical spacetime separation, graph distance in every carrier, or the phase displacement along an F orbit. The distance must be compatible with the allowed handoff interfaces and the history whose slope is being measured.

An internal event can leave field address unchanged. A same-address return can retain nontrivial orientation or history. Conversely two records can lie outside a phase-only readout's comparison domain even when a native graph edge connects them. The retained G9000 report makes that limitation explicit.

terms.title: Thalean c and causal slope of becoming
terms.status: D; P conditional on locality and saturation; physical calibration F
terms.section: VII. Event depth, field reach, time, and recurrence
terms.body:
Thalean c is the maximal causal slope of an admitted event-preserving history:

```text
c_Th = sup_gamma d_field(s(gamma),t(gamma)) / |gamma|_event
c_Th = 1
```

The locked datum is dimensionless. Its preferred reading is "one transmission per relationship per event," meaning at most one new adjacent field address per primitive event step, with complete recoverable accounting. "One event per event" remains a mnemonic, not an independent derivation.

Under the declared per-step locality bound, the triangle inequality gives the upper bound. An admitted depth-one address-changing handoff supplies saturation. This does not claim that every long path saturates, that every internal operation propagates, or that recurrence frequency equals causal speed.

No conversion to meters and seconds follows. The definition is retained unless a native theorem or failed audit forces revision, while physical calibration remains separate.

terms.title: Thalean time
terms.status: D/P on the declared registered-history domain
terms.section: VII. Event depth, field reach, time, and recurrence
terms.body:
Thalean time is the primitive additive oriented winding of the distinguished G30-visible registered-history cycle r1 in its certified cycle register. Its immediate domain is admitted closed registered histories; extension to open paths requires the relevant reference and comparison data.

```text
tau_Th(gamma) = wind_(r1)(gamma)
tau_Th(gamma2 o gamma1) = tau_Th(gamma2) + tau_Th(gamma1)
tau_Th(gamma^-1) = -tau_Th(gamma)
```

Time is downstream of registered becoming in this formulation. It is not defined as every update, every appended record, loss of freedom, rising complexity, or recurrence phase. A history can change while a particular scalar winding does not.

The symbol r1 also appears in separate involution/parent discussions. Equal names do not identify a cycle class with a group element. Use the source's domain-qualified notation. Physical proper time remains a correspondence target.

terms.title: Thalean tick
terms.status: D
terms.section: VII. Event depth, field reach, time, and recurrence
terms.body:
A Thalean tick is one positively oriented primitive traversal of the distinguished registered-history cycle, normalized by Delta tau_Th=+1.

It is not generally one graph edge, one transducer operation, one primitive handoff, or one second. Several event steps can participate in one tick, and an event can occur without adding positive winding in the selected time register.

The source's distinction "event step != time tick" is therefore retained as a typed boundary. A particular realization can prove a relationship between the two counts, but that relationship must be stated rather than assumed from the word "event." The tick is an oriented history unit, whereas execution depth is nonnegative compositional cost.

terms.title: Recurrence, eigenphase, and frequency
terms.status: D/C; physical frequency requires parameter calibration
terms.section: VII. Event depth, field reach, time, and recurrence
terms.body:
Recurrence is return under a specified state action, phase representation, or orbit. Eigenphase is the phase associated with an eigenvalue of a specified update. A frequency or omega becomes a rate only relative to a declared evolution parameter.

These are not the same as empirical outcome frequency, which is a ratio of registered counts. Nor is recurrence rate the causal datum c_Th or the additive winding tau_Th. A finite F orbit with period twenty gives a return law, not a clock calibrated in seconds and not a nonperiodic outcome source.

Every use should identify its carrier and parameter: visible-state recurrence, complete finite-state recurrence, modal C3 phase, pure C5 frame phase, and registered C20 phase have different meanings. The common divisor or equal numerical angle supplies no state-action intertwiner.

terms.title: Finite carrier and extensible history
terms.status: D/P as an architecture; native controller use requires coupling
terms.section: VII. Event depth, field reach, time, and recurrence
terms.body:
A fixed finite carrier can support arbitrarily long finite words of admitted actions. The set of its current vertices is finite; the length of an accumulated ordered history need not have a fixed bound. "The Thalion is finite. Becoming is not" is the mnemonic for this distinction, not a claim that infinitely many vertices fit inside the object.

A complete state that includes an unbounded retained register is not itself a fixed finite state space. This matters when evaluating proposed frequency generators. A passive unbounded log does not change a finite autonomous controller's future unless the controller reads it.

The archive distinguishes finite endpoint state, stored word, sufficient predictive state, and scalar history readout. Each can discard different information. Repetition of the endpoint need not repeat the log, while an identical log summary need not identify the whole history.

terms.title: Finite-state irrational-frequency boundary
terms.status: P under the stated deterministic autonomy assumptions
terms.section: VII. Event depth, field reach, time, and recurrence
terms.body:
An autonomous deterministic process whose complete internal state ranges over one fixed finite set is eventually periodic. If each step contributes a fixed finite registered output, its limiting branch frequencies are rational.

This excludes obtaining an exact irrational Born frequency merely by cycling through the currently certified finite G60/G900/G1800/G9000 endpoint states. It does not exclude irrational eigenvalues or normalized spectral masses of finite matrices. Spectral arithmetic and chronological frequency generation are different theorem fronts.

A literal nonperiodic frequency realization therefore needs additional structure outside that finite-autonomous model, such as an actively used unbounded history register, non-autonomous input, or a stochastic law. Listing those possibilities does not select one as native. The source law must still be independently constructed and connected to registration.

terms.title: Thalean freedom
terms.status: D/H; rank requires a declared independence structure
terms.section: VIII. Freedom, carry-forward, and finite-frame opportunity
terms.body:
Thalean freedom is the dimensionality of permissible action after the active relational constraints are applied. The adopted emphasis is that freedom is measured in independent degrees, not merely in the number of labels or outcomes.

```text
F_Th(x | Ctx,Ref) = dim P(x | Ctx,Ref)
d_Th(z) = rank P_z
```

These expressions require an actual linear space, module, or other specified independence/rank structure. They do not assign a canonical dimension to an arbitrary finite successor set. The reference supplies coordinates for describing permission; it does not create freedom.

Local freedom can rise or fall along a history. The monotonicity of a fixed completion family is a different statement. The glossary therefore does not identify local rank with residual log-count freedom, relational complexity, time, or information preserved in the complete output.

terms.title: One degree of freedom
terms.status: D/H; construction-dependent realization
terms.section: VIII. Freedom, carry-forward, and finite-frame opportunity
terms.body:
One Thalean degree of freedom is one independent admissible action direction remaining after the declared constraints. A value F_Th=1 means one such independent direction, not necessarily exactly one labeled future event.

Several possible outcomes can lie along one degree, and several registered representatives can encode the same direction. Conversely two superficially similar branches can be independent when the admitted action structure says so. Independence must be exhibited, not inferred by dividing a state count.

A forced unique successor and a zero-dimensional choice parameter can coincide in a particular parametrization, but they are not universal synonyms. This entry keeps the user's "freedom is measured in degrees" precise while leaving the native permissible-action structure as a carrier-specific construction task.

terms.title: Finite-frame continuation family
terms.status: D; exact nesting within a fixed frame
terms.section: VIII. Freedom, carry-forward, and finite-frame opportunity
terms.body:
For a declared finite frame W, let Omega_W be its fixed set of complete allowed histories. At a realized prefix h, the continuation family is:

```text
C_W(h) = {w in Omega_W : h is a prefix of w}
```

After an admitted extension e, C_W(h e) is a subset of C_W(h). The comparison uses the same complete-history universe and the same horizon. Extending the horizon, changing apparatus, or redefining the completion set changes the problem and cannot be used inside the same monotonicity claim.

This object counts compatible completions, not local independent directions. Histories differing only by redundant lift labels must be handled under the stated counting convention. An empty family means the prefix is incompatible with the chosen frame, not that an ordinary finite logarithmic freedom value has been reached.

terms.title: Residual finite-frame freedom
terms.status: D; P for monotonicity of the defined count
terms.section: VIII. Freedom, carry-forward, and finite-frame opportunity
terms.body:
Residual finite-frame freedom is the logarithm of the number of surviving completions in a fixed nonempty finite completion family:

```text
F_W(h) = log |C_W(h)|
F_W(h e) <= F_W(h)
```

The logarithm base must be fixed; choosing base two expresses the count in binary information-like units, not in the same unit as a vector-space dimension. The inequality follows from inclusion of prefix-compatible completion sets.

An event can have equality. For example, when every surviving completion begins with the same next event, appending it removes no completion. Consequently this quantity is not Thalean time and does not prove that every action spends freedom. Local action rank can increase even while this fixed-frame completion count decreases.

terms.title: Resolved freedom
terms.status: D; relative to a fixed initial prefix
terms.section: VIII. Freedom, carry-forward, and finite-frame opportunity
terms.body:
Resolved freedom measures the decrease in residual completion log-count from a declared initial prefix h0:

```text
R_W(h) = F_W(h0) - F_W(h)
```

It records how much of the original finite family has been excluded by the actual prefix. It is nondecreasing under the same fixed-frame assumptions that make F_W nonincreasing. It is not a universal amount of action, elapsed time, or destroyed information.

The word "resolved" refers to alternative completions no longer compatible with this history. It does not imply that every formerly available task or degree has been permanently lost; some can carry forward in a different ordering. Distinguish this logarithmic count from rank loss under a carry-forward map and from the operational notion of opportunity cost.

terms.title: Carry-forward map
terms.status: H/C when source and target action spaces are supplied
terms.section: VIII. Freedom, carry-forward, and finite-frame opportunity
terms.body:
A carry-forward map kappa_e represents how permissible action directions before an event survive as permissible directions afterward. It must be derived for the actual event and declared source/target action spaces, not chosen merely to make a freedom-loss formula work.

Within a linear rank formulation, the candidate expenditure is:

```text
loss_e = dim P(h) - rank(kappa_e)
```

This measures old directions not carried forward. It does not determine how many new directions become available after the event, and it does not assert that the complete transduction loses information when kappa_e loses rank. The two maps have different domains and purposes.

A nontrivial event can preserve the rank of kappa_e, giving zero expenditure by this measure. The formula is a proposed formalization on supplied action spaces, not a universal theorem for every Thalean carrier.

terms.title: Thalean opportunity cost and freedom expenditure
terms.status: D/H; analogy is operational, not an imported economic model
terms.section: VIII. Freedom, carry-forward, and finite-frame opportunity
terms.body:
Thalean opportunity cost is admissible action capacity that fails to carry forward because an event was realized. It is not simply the number of alternatives that were not chosen at that instant, and it is not the mere fact that another occurrence entered the log.

Some opportunities can remain available after a different action. The correct question is whether the relevant degree or task survives in the subsequent admissible family, under the declared comparison. An alternative past ordering can be foreclosed while a future opportunity remains.

This makes precise the user's observation that some possibilities carry forward without cost. It also preserves "freedom can be spent; information cannot be discarded": capacity to choose can decrease while the complete output retains the information needed to account for that decrease. No identification with temperature or time is implied.

terms.title: Forced event
terms.status: D; context-specific determination
terms.section: VIII. Freedom, carry-forward, and finite-frame opportunity
terms.body:
A forced event is a realized event whose next continuation is uniquely determined at the declared level of admissibility. It can add an occurrence and a receipt without further reducing the compatible completion family.

A forced event may participate in positive time winding, zero winding, or another registered history change depending on its cycle register. The freedom discussion uses this to refute the equation "time is freedom resolution": time can advance without positive freedom expenditure. It does not claim every forced event is itself one tick.

Uniqueness is context-dependent. A projected state can appear to allow two branches while a supplied richer context permits one, but such richer determination must be shown rather than presumed. Forcedness does not follow from knowing the outcome after registration.

terms.title: Continuation multiplicity
terms.status: D/C for a declared counting grammar
terms.section: VIII. Freedom, carry-forward, and finite-frame opportunity
terms.body:
Continuation multiplicity is the number of distinct admitted continuation words over a specified depth and counting convention. For a finite matrix A_cont counting labeled transitions or their declared multiplicities:

```text
N_L(i) = (A_cont^L 1)_i
```

The baseline used "number, weight, or dimension" broadly. This edition keeps literal multiplicity as the counting notion and explicitly names weighted measure or dimension when those different quantities are intended. They cannot be compared without a conversion rule.

A regular cover can supply several lifts of the same base path. That is a carrier multiplicity, not automatically a fresh independent choice at every step. The initial lift can determine the later lift uniquely. The native status of A_cont must be established separately from the usefulness of the formula.

terms.title: Continuation entropy
terms.status: D/C on a supplied continuation language
terms.section: VIII. Freedom, carry-forward, and finite-frame opportunity
terms.body:
Continuation entropy is a declared measure of variation or asymptotic growth in admitted future words. The manuscript uses the exponential language-growth rate:

```text
h_cont(i) = limsup_(L->infinity) (1/L) log N_L(i)
```

Multiplying every path count by one fixed finite covering factor does not change this rate. That is the precise boundary behind "deck multiplicity != dynamical multiplicity." It does not mean lifted states never matter; a lift-sensitive interaction can make them operationally distinct.

This growth rate is not the finite-frame log-count F_W(h), a physical thermodynamic entropy, or a universal count of free dimensions. Direct sums do not automatically establish tensor-product branching. Always state the language, quotient convention, and normalization before interpreting an entropy value.

terms.title: G60, G30, and G15
terms.status: D/P as inherited finite carriers
terms.section: IX. Native carrier, quotient, and routing vocabulary
terms.body:
G60 denotes the 60-state Thalion carrier AT4val[60,6]. In the inherited tower, G30 is its named two-fold quotient and G15 is the quotient by the native free Klein-four register. The G15 carrier is identified with the line graph of the Petersen graph in the retained construction.

These are different domains, not different numerical resolutions of one unspecified matrix. A function or action descends only when it is compatible with the relevant fibers. A statement established on G15 need not retain the signed-lift information present at G60.

The broader census-family work also uses Q30, a shared family intermediate, distinct from the inherited G30. Its appearance in a cover diagram does not rename G30. Every quotient equation should include the actual map or kernel being used. The object name Thalion remains attached to the G60 form, not to any of these shadows.

terms.title: Native Klein register and local orientation cell
terms.status: D/P on the named native register
terms.section: IX. Native carrier, quotient, and routing vocabulary
terms.body:
The native Klein register is V4 = {1,a,b,ab}, a free normal four-element action in the inherited G60 construction. A local orientation cell is one four-state fiber of that action. The three nonidentity involutions are the three pairings of its four elements, abstractly the perfect matchings of K4.

On this register a^2 = b^2 = 1 and ab = ba. The notation ab is the product in this particular Klein action. It does not imply that arbitrary lifted actors in every larger carrier commute. Conversely, noncommuting lifts elsewhere do not retroactively make native Klein multiplication noncommutative.

The cell is relational rather than an assigned Euclidean coordinate frame. In particular a is not defined as a cubic centroid. Other V4 groups, including a quotient of a rooted D8 or a voltage-label group, require their own crosswalk to this native register.

terms.title: Native register-orientation character
terms.status: P reported in native symmetry sources
terms.section: IX. Native carrier, quotient, and routing vocabulary
terms.body:
The full native G60 conjugation action distinguishes a from the pair {b,ab}. Its image on the named Klein register is C2: a is fixed, while b and ab are either both fixed or exchanged.

terms.title: Relational measure

terms.body:

Measure is distinct from a count of observed outcomes and from the process generating the next outcome. It can be structurally specified before a chronological sequence is available. The glossary therefore retains three separate questions: what fixes the weights, what records their realizations, and what generates the history. A measure also requires its counting or reference convention; equal state counts, equal amplitudes, and equal spectral trace masses are not interchangeable preparations.

terms.title: Born mass and spectral weight

The history construction gives (5 +/- sqrt(5))/10 for its two six-dimensional sectors. The four-cell refinement gives (5 +/- sqrt(5))/20, twice each. The frame-current candidate reproduces these numbers through a different construction, still awaiting its native history intertwiner.

The Program 03 branch supplies a reported finite registration construction with context-local counting and discrepancy control for a fixed input measure. Its scope is not that any weak microscopic instrument can be repaired by recording more carefully. Changing the outcome probabilities changes the measurement rather than faithfully registering it.

The source and instrument must therefore be specified upstream. Event ordering, setting interleaving, null outcomes, leakage, and any herald must be accounted for in the actual construction. An ideal registered table and a physically implemented instrument remain different levels of completion.

terms.title: Probability as registered relational readout

terms.section: XI. Measure, probability, preparation, and Born/EPR readout

The working QR interpretation does not require probability to be a primitive command consulted by an individual event. It seeks probability as relational measure made legible through registered histories and their empirical frequencies. The retained shorthand is: law resides in permissible action; probability is read from history.

This is not a claim that a mathematical probability can only be calculated after an event, nor that every possible source must be deterministic. A measure can be evaluated prospectively, and the native source may ultimately require retained history, non-autonomous inputs, or a stochastic law.

The singularity of an actual recorded outcome does not by itself establish a hidden trajectory, an outcome-selection mechanism, or the absence of coherent alternatives. Keep the interpretive thesis separate from the exact finite spectral masses and from the operational assumptions used to register them.

The retained Program 03 report is imported as a stronger full four-cell construction rather than inferred from a simple binary example. A discrepancy bound is a theorem about the declared sequence generator and counting rule; it does not supply an independently native source.

Exact irrational limiting weights are compatible with unbounded history-based constructions even though a closed finite deterministic recurrence has rational limiting frequencies. That distinction is not resolved by appending a log which the controller never reads. Frequency, spectral mass, recurrence frequency, and physical angular frequency require different labels.

terms.title: Source provenance and process provenance
terms.status: D; native selection and chronology remain construction-specific
terms.section: XI. Measure, probability, preparation, and Born/EPR readout
terms.body:
Source provenance specifies how an input state, preparation, or retained control is constructed from admitted data. Process provenance specifies the law producing the actual sequence of continuations and receipts. They answer different parts of "where did this registered history come from?"

A vector belonging to a native carrier is not automatically a reachable preparation. A deterministic sequence reproducing a target histogram is not automatically the native chronology. A passive log can preserve past events without influencing the next one.

The Born frontier therefore includes an independently sourced preparation and evolving-history rule, not merely another proof that a target measure is realizable. Source choices must be fixed before optimizing the desired correlation or weights. This glossary preserves proposed controls and their reported failures without replacing provenance by a fitted scheduler.

terms.title: Registration nonamplification
terms.status: D/P as the declared information-processing constraint
terms.section: XI. Measure, probability, preparation, and Born/EPR readout
terms.body:
A faithful downstream registrar cannot create a distinction absent from the complete upstream output available to it. When two alternatives induce exactly the same available data, any deterministic function of those data also agrees. A richer interaction can distinguish them only by accessing additional information or performing a new transduction.

This is why registration cannot repair a weak instrument. It can preserve, summarize, or reveal a distinction already present in its inputs, but it cannot legitimately change a deficient upstream outcome measure while claiming to record the same measurement.

Distinguish this operational statement from a scalar "visibility" diagnostic. A changed readout can improve usefulness when it uses additional available information, but then its resources and admissible interface must be stated. No frequency counter or downstream history layer supplies a missing physical analyzer coupling by itself.

terms.title: Preparation, instrument, and operational readout
terms.status: D; native and physical realization require their own evidence

terms.body:
A preparation is an admitted process producing the input before the relevant measurement choices. An instrument is the admitted setting-dependent interaction and outcome-resolved update. A readout maps its available output to records; a pointer is the explicit register carrying those records.

A projector, a positive normalized effect family, and an implementable instrument are distinct objects. A physical preparation additionally needs an apparatus correspondence, not just a state selected in a calculation. A herald marks a declared readiness condition; its timing and outcome accounting cannot be silently chosen after the settings or successful detections are known.

All branches relevant to normalization must remain visible, including null outcomes and leakage. The prior apparatus work specifically separates a clean/excursion coordinate from an actual ready/written pointer. Reusing a convenient two-state label is not proof that the measurement record has been implemented.

However, unbiased marginals alone neither establish entanglement nor identify the operational assumptions of a Bell experiment. Preparation, setting independence, complete outcome accounting, and the admissible local interfaces must also be specified.

The proposed quantum reading emphasizes alternatives, noncommuting observables, phase, composition, measure, and registered outcomes. Both are sought as reductions of the same information-preserving transducer architecture.

The minimal criterion is structural: a common native invariant or carrier relation must feed both readings through independently constructed maps without changing the underlying law. A shared number, dimension, group order, or visual analogy is not enough.

Even a common invariant is a milestone rather than sufficient proof of all of quantum mechanics and general relativity. A full physical reduction needs its state spaces, operations, preparation, instruments, locality, dynamics, calibration, and controlled limits. Neither QM-as-GR nor GR-as-QM is assumed. This entry retains the baseline's complementary-reading thesis with the manuscript's stricter correspondence boundary.

A conversation checkpoint preserves a claim and its context even before a producer artifact has been recovered. That is valuable archival evidence but must not be relabeled as a fresh computation. The archive discussion adds a practical bootstrapping goal: preserve the definitions, decoding conventions, native data, and validation route needed to recover the account. Physical media proposals and institutional metaphors do not add physics axioms. This update is an indexed archival consolidation, not a new admission or repository seal.
